questions.stem: A regulator raises concern about repeated boundary violations. What should the organisation do?

options.text: Review policy, education, supervision, reporting and cultural factors across the service.
Remove all patient contact from staff.

questions.rationale: A pattern requires governance-level analysis and response.

questions.sectionLabel: Governance, Regulation and Professional Quality Improvement
questions.stem: Which outcome best indicates professional governance maturity?

options.text: Competence is verified, data drive action and standards are reliably translated into practice.
Complaints are low because reporting is difficult.

questions.rationale: Mature governance connects oversight with measurable practice change.

questions.sectionLabel: Governance, Regulation and Professional Quality Improvement
questions.stem: Which outcome best reflects the Level 3 governance role?

options.text: The nurse delegates governance to regulators.
The nurse helps identify professional-risk trends, strengthen competence systems and evaluate improvement.

questions.rationale: Global Nursing Professionals contribute actively to governance and public protection.

questions.sectionLabel: Ethical Practice in Digital Health, Research and Innovation
questions.stem: A predictive tool repeatedly assigns lower risk to a minority population despite concerning clinical findings. What should nurse leaders do?

options.text: Document the pattern, suspend unsafe reliance and initiate a bias and governance review.
Continue using the score because it is automated.
Ask staff to trust the tool.
Exclude the population from the tool.

questions.rationale: Technology must be critically appraised and monitored for bias and harm.

questions.sectionLabel: Ethical Practice in Digital Health, Research and Innovation
questions.stem: Which statement best describes digital professionalism?

options.text: Electronic communication may be less formal than face-to-face care.
Digital communication should remain respectful, secure and clinically appropriate.
Copying records saves time and is always acceptable.
Accessing records for learning is permitted.

questions.rationale: Professional duties apply in every medium.

questions.sectionLabel: Ethical Practice in Digital Health, Research and Innovation
questions.stem: A nurse accesses a celebrity patient's record without a care-related need. What has occurred?
questions.rationale: Information should be accessed only for legitimate purposes.

questions.sectionLabel: Ethical Practice in Digital Health, Research and Innovation
questions.stem: Which risk is associated with copying electronic records forward?

options.text: Outdated or incorrect information may be perpetuated.

questions.rationale: Copying may compromise data integrity and clinical safety.

questions.sectionLabel: Ethical Practice in Digital Health, Research and Innovation
questions.stem: A decision-support system recommends a medicine that conflicts with the patient's allergy history. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Apply clinical judgement, withhold administration and escalate the discrepancy.

questions.rationale: Technology supports but does not replace professional judgement.

questions.sectionLabel: Ethical Practice in Digital Health, Research and Innovation
questions.stem: Which principle requires research participants to receive adequate information and choose voluntarily?

options.text: Respect for persons and informed consent.

questions.rationale: Ethical research requires informed and voluntary participation.

questions.sectionLabel: Ethical Practice in Digital Health, Research and Innovation
questions.stem: A research project exposes participants to avoidable harm without sufficient benefit. Which principle is breached?
questions.rationale: Research ethics requires risks to be minimised and justified.

questions.sectionLabel: Ethical Practice in Digital Health, Research and Innovation
questions.stem: Why is independent ethical review important?

options.text: It is required only for drug trials.
It provides oversight of consent, fairness, risk and participant protection.

questions.rationale: Independent review supports trust and participant protection.

questions.sectionLabel: Ethical Practice in Digital Health, Research and Innovation
questions.stem: A researcher pressures dependent patients to enrol. What is the main ethical concern?

options.text: Voluntariness may be compromised by power imbalance.
The sample may be too small.

questions.rationale: Participation must be free from coercion or undue influence.

questions.sectionLabel: Ethical Practice in Digital Health, Research and Innovation
questions.stem: Which action best protects research privacy?

options.text: Limiting access, securing data and using information only for approved purposes.

questions.rationale: Privacy and data integrity are core research obligations.

questions.sectionLabel: Ethical Practice in Digital Health, Research and Innovation
questions.stem: A new AI system is introduced without patient involvement or post-implementation monitoring. What is the main governance weakness?

options.text: Innovation lacks participation, accountability and safety surveillance.
Monitoring is needed only after an incident.

questions.rationale: Innovation should be tested, monitored and reviewed with patient involvement and clear accountability.

questions.sectionLabel: Ethical Practice in Digital Health, Research and Innovation
questions.stem: Which measure is most useful for monitoring a new digital tool?

options.text: Accuracy, bias, privacy incidents, overrides, unintended harm and patient experience.

questions.rationale: Evaluation should include safety, equity, use and experience.

questions.sectionLabel: Ethical Practice in Digital Health, Research and Innovation
questions.stem: A digital consent system is difficult for people with low literacy. What should leaders do?

options.text: Provide accessible alternatives and monitor meaningful participation.
Ask family members to complete it.
Exclude those unable to use it.

questions.rationale: Innovation must support equitable, informed participation.

questions.sectionLabel: Ethical Practice in Digital Health, Research and Innovation
questions.stem: Which statement best reflects accountability for AI-supported decisions?

options.text: The AI vendor holds all accountability.
Clinicians remain responsible for critical appraisal and escalation.
The patient accepts the risk by using the system.
Accountability is shared so no one is individually responsible.

questions.rationale: Professional accountability is not transferred to technology.

questions.sectionLabel: Ethical Practice in Digital Health, Research and Innovation
questions.stem: A clinical trial recruits only populations with easy access but claims broad benefit. Which ethical concern is most relevant?

options.text: Fairness and justice in participant selection and applicability.

questions.rationale: Research ethics includes fair selection and distribution of burdens and benefits.

questions.sectionLabel: Ethical Practice in Digital Health, Research and Innovation
questions.stem: A researcher discovers a serious protocol deviation. What should happen?

options.text: Hide it to protect the study.
Report it through the approved research-governance process and protect participants.

questions.rationale: Research integrity requires transparency and participant protection.

questions.sectionLabel: Ethical Practice in Digital Health, Research and Innovation
questions.stem: Which action best supports responsible innovation?

options.text: Pilot, evaluate, involve patients, protect privacy and define accountability.
Use the system without override options.

questions.rationale: Innovation governance must address ethical and technical performance.

questions.sectionLabel: Ethical Practice in Digital Health, Research and Innovation
questions.stem: A nurse identifies that an algorithm's recommendation differs from the patient's condition. What should be documented?

options.text: The clinical findings, algorithm output, reasoning, escalation and action taken.

questions.rationale: Transparent documentation supports accountability and learning.

questions.sectionLabel: Ethical Practice in Digital Health, Research and Innovation
questions.stem: Which outcome best demonstrates ethical digital health?

options.text: Technology improves care while preserving judgement, privacy, fairness and informed participation.

questions.rationale: Ethical digital practice balances benefit with rights and accountability.

questions.sectionLabel: Ethical Practice in Digital Health, Research and Innovation
questions.stem: Which outcome best reflects the Level 3 role in research and innovation?

options.text: The nurse uses new tools confidently.
The nurse leaves ethics to researchers.
The nurse focuses only on technical performance.
The nurse evaluates evidence, identifies ethical risks and strengthens governance before and after implementation.

questions.rationale: Global Nursing Professionals guide responsible and trustworthy innovation.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Professional Standards, Advocacy and the Future of Nursing
questions.stem: Which values provide common ground across different nursing systems?

options.text: Dignity, safety, fairness, confidentiality and accountability.

questions.rationale: Global values may be shared even when legal and cultural contexts differ.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Professional Standards, Advocacy and the Future of Nursing
questions.stem: A service identifies that a digital-only appointment system disadvantages older adults. What should leaders do?

options.text: Introduce accessible alternatives and monitor participation across groups.

questions.rationale: Professional advocacy includes equitable participation and access.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Professional Standards, Advocacy and the Future of Nursing
questions.stem: Which action best demonstrates advocacy for human rights?

options.text: Identifying discrimination and changing systems that restrict dignity, access or participation.
Focusing only on individual bedside care.

questions.rationale: Global professionalism includes advocacy for ethical systems and vulnerable populations.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Professional Standards, Advocacy and the Future of Nursing
questions.stem: A global guideline conflicts with local law. What should the nurse leader do?

options.text: Follow the guideline because it is international.
Apply shared values while adapting practice to lawful local requirements.

questions.rationale: Global values must be applied within local legal and cultural context.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Professional Standards, Advocacy and the Future of Nursing
questions.stem: Which factor most strongly supports public trust?
questions.rationale: Trust depends on safe practice and transparent responsibility.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Professional Standards, Advocacy and the Future of Nursing
questions.stem: A nurse mentor notices a colleague repeatedly avoiding reflection after errors. What is the best approach?

options.text: Use constructive feedback, supported reflection and clear accountability expectations.

questions.rationale: Mentoring should combine respect, learning and professional standards.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Professional Standards, Advocacy and the Future of Nursing
questions.stem: Which mentoring behaviour is most effective?

options.text: Using questions, feedback and reflection to help the colleague reason independently.

questions.rationale: Mentoring develops professional judgement, not dependence.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Professional Standards, Advocacy and the Future of Nursing
questions.stem: A workforce-development programme uses examples from one cultural setting only. What should leaders do?

options.text: Include diverse contexts and examine how global values apply locally.

questions.rationale: Global professional education should be culturally relevant while preserving common values.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Professional Standards, Advocacy and the Future of Nursing
questions.stem: Which equity concern should professional leaders monitor?

options.text: Differences in access and outcomes related to discrimination, geography, disability or social disadvantage.

questions.rationale: The notes explicitly link advocacy to discrimination, access and vulnerable populations.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Professional Standards, Advocacy and the Future of Nursing
questions.stem: A service receives evidence that its complaint process is inaccessible to low-literacy patients. What should leaders do?

options.text: Co-design accessible alternatives and monitor who can use the system.
Maintain the process to ensure consistency.

questions.rationale: Public trust requires meaningful access to accountability processes.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Professional Standards, Advocacy and the Future of Nursing
questions.stem: Which statement best reflects lifelong learning?

options.text: Professional capability requires continuing education, reflection and feedback.

questions.rationale: Standards evolve, so competence must be maintained throughout practice.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Professional Standards, Advocacy and the Future of Nursing
questions.stem: A global nursing partnership proposes importing a governance model unchanged. What should local leaders do?

options.text: Adapt the model to local law, culture, resources and workforce while preserving core ethical values.

questions.rationale: Global learning should be adapted rather than copied mechanically.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Professional Standards, Advocacy and the Future of Nursing
questions.stem: Which outcome best demonstrates effective professional advocacy?

options.text: An inequitable process is changed and access improves for affected populations.

questions.rationale: Advocacy should lead to measurable system improvement.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Professional Standards, Advocacy and the Future of Nursing
questions.stem: A leader withholds information about a serious system failure to protect reputation. What is the greatest professional risk?

options.text: Loss of public trust due to lack of honesty and accountability.

questions.rationale: Transparency and visible accountability are foundations of trust.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Professional Standards, Advocacy and the Future of Nursing
questions.stem: Which action best supports future professional standards?

options.text: Use evidence, emerging risks, lived experience and global learning to update standards responsibly.

questions.rationale: Professional standards should evolve while preserving core values.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Professional Standards, Advocacy and the Future of Nursing
questions.stem: A nurse leader identifies systemic discrimination but fears organisational resistance. What should the leader do?

options.text: Use evidence, advocacy and appropriate governance channels to pursue change.

questions.rationale: Ethical leadership includes challenging unfair systems.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Professional Standards, Advocacy and the Future of Nursing
questions.stem: Which outcome best reflects global professional integrity?

options.text: Shared ethical values are applied transparently within local context.
All countries use the same rules.

questions.rationale: Integrity combines common values with context-sensitive lawful practice.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Professional Standards, Advocacy and the Future of Nursing
questions.stem: A mentor gives feedback that focuses only on weaknesses. What should be improved?

options.text: Feedback should identify strengths, specific gaps and practical next steps.
Only formal assessment should be used.
The mentor should compare the nurse with peers.

questions.rationale: Constructive mentoring is respectful, balanced and action-oriented.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Professional Standards, Advocacy and the Future of Nursing
questions.stem: Which measure best reflects public trust?

options.text: Patient confidence, transparent complaint response, competence data and visible accountability.

questions.rationale: Trust should be evaluated through experience and organisational behaviour.

questions.sectionLabel: Global Professional Standards, Advocacy and the Future of Nursing
questions.stem: Which outcome best reflects the Level 3 global professional role?

options.text: The nurse practises ethically as an individual.
The nurse focuses on international travel.
The nurse mentors others, advocates for equity and helps standards evolve while protecting public trust.

questions.rationale: Global Nursing Professionals influence culture, systems and future standards.
